sentences.text: Lomasuchus featured a deep, narrow snout typical of its family, along with compressed, serrated teeth that were less flattened than those of its relative Peirosaurus.
Gasparini and colleagues named the genus in 1991 based on the single known fossil, the holotype specimen MOZ 4084 PV, discovered at the Loma de la Lata locality in Patagonia.
This reptile belongs to the family Peirosauridae, and the genus Lomasuchus gives its name to the subfamily Lomasuchinae within that group.

Although the Paleobiology Database lists its time range as the Turonian to Coniacian stages, recent studies place this reptile in the Santonian-age Bajo de la Carpa Formation of Neuquén Province, western central Argentina.
